effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the Cryptarchia Proof of Leadership specification, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence' (the compiled circuit is external evidence). Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-pol, logos-blockchain-core, logos-blockchain-ledger or logos-blockchain-chain-leader-service that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is the LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot).

Where the specification lives in the code:
- zk/proofs/pol/src (package `logos-blockchain-pol`): the proof of leadership. inputs.rs, chain_inputs.rs and wallet_inputs.rs are the public and private inputs; witness.rs builds the circuit witness; lottery.rs the lottery threshold computation (the stake-dependent threshold and its fixed-point arithmetic); lib.rs proving and verification. The circuit itself is the prebuilt crate `lbc-pol-sys` (feature `prebuilt`), outside the repository; what the circuit constrains is visible only through the public inputs and the verification key, so a divergence inside the circuit is 'needs external evidence'.
- core/src/proofs/leader_proof.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): `LeaderPublic`, the public inputs as the block header carries them, and the verification entry point. core/src/proofs/mod.rs.
- ledger/src/cryptarchia/mod.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): where the ledger checks a header's leader proof against the epoch state (nonce, stake snapshot, total stake, lottery parameters) and the slot.
- services/chain/chain-leader/src/leadership.rs (package `logos-blockchain-chain-leader-service`): the prover side, how a leader finds a winning note and builds the proof.
- Adjacent, outside the unit: zk/groth16 and zk/circuits/verifier (the verifier, its own LIPs), the Cryptarchia Protocol LIP (lottery parameters lottery_0 and lottery_1, audited by another brief).

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. Proving is slow (the pol crate has a `prove` benchmark); a proof test that needs a real proof should prove once. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
effective.gate: cargo nextest run --locked -p logos-blockchain-pol -p logos-blockchain-core -p logos-blockchain-ledger -p logos-blockchain-chain-leader-service --all-features --no-fail-fast
